question_text: Find the pole of ax + by + c = 0 with respect to x² + y² = r².

mark_split.label: Write the polar of the unknown pole
Compare and read off the pole

insider_note: The answer is a formula, not a number, so the letters must be carried through — and c cannot be zero, because a line through the centre has no pole.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the polar of the unknown pole
steps.margin_note: One mark. For a circle centred at the origin the polar is short: x₁x + y₁y − r² = 0.
steps.memory_tip: Polar of P(x₁, y₁) with respect to x² + y² = r² is x₁x + y₁y = r².
lines: Let P(x₁, y₁) be the pole of ax + by + c = 0.
The polar of P with respect to x² + y² = r²
steps.why: With the centre at the origin there are no linear terms in the circle, so S₁ reduces to x₁x + y₁y − r². The pole is whatever point makes that line the given one.
common_mistakes: Writing the polar as xx₁ + yy₁ + r² = 0.
Adding g and f terms that an origin-centred circle does not have.

steps.label: Compare and read off the pole
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Comparing gives the answer at once; no letter k is needed for a two-term polar.
lines: This is the same line as ax + by + c = 0, so
steps.why: Two equations describe the same line when their coefficients are proportional. The constant of the polar is −r² and the constant of the given line is c, so the common ratio is −r²/c.
common_mistakes: Writing the ratio as r²/c and losing the minus sign.
Treating c as the radius because of the letter.
